newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean think-tank ups '97 GDP growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean think-tank ups '97 GDP growth forecast.

text.p: The state-run Korea Development Institute (KDI) has revised upward its forecast for this year's real gross domestic product (GDP) growth to 6.2 percent from 6.0 percent, a KDI report said on Wednesday.
The institute's earlier forecast was given in April.
The central Bank of Korea on Monday put its 1997 GDP growth forecast at 6.0 percent against 7.1 percent in calendar 1996.
KDI attributed the revision to an easing of the Japanese yen's fall against the dollar and stablising financial markets following labour strife and the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co earlier this year.
The KDI report also predicted this year's current account deficit at $16.2 billion, down from its earlier forecast of a $19.6 billion shortfall.
It said a fall in raw material import costs and a halt in the yen's decline were expected to cap the rising deficit.
The central bank has forecast this year's current account deficit at $17 billion, against last year's $23.7 billion.
KDI reduced its forecast for the 1997 customs-cleared trade deficit to $6.8 billion from an earlier $11.8 billion. It expected South Korea to turn to a $500 million surplus in the last quarter.
The government has earlier forecast a $14 billion trade deficit for this year, against a $20.62 billion shortfall in 1996.
The institute lowered the forecast for consumer price index (CPI) growth to 4.5 percent this year from an earlier projection of 4.7 percent.
The report cited the recent stable exchange rate and a drop in international raw material prices as the reasons behind the downgrade.
